title: Quantitative Tor bounds under shifts and isomorphisms on the pro-etale site
statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme and $A$ an arbitrary commutative ring. Work on the small pro-etale site $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with its constant sheaf of rings $A_Y$ and the unbounded derived category $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Use the K-flat derived tensor product [def-weil-derived-tensor] and cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. For every $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, every sheaf $N$ of $A_Y$-modules placed in degree zero, and integers $i,m$, there are isomorphisms, natural in $K$ and $N$,
$$
 (K[m])\otimes_A^L N\cong(K\otimes_A^L N)[m],\qquad
 \mathcal H^i((K[m])\otimes_A^L N)\cong\mathcal H^{i+m}(K\otimes_A^L N).
$$
For any integers $a\leq b$, $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ if and only if $K[m]$ has Tor amplitude in $[a-m,b-m]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. If $K\cong L$, then $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ if and only if $L$ does. Moreover $0\otimes_A^L N\cong0$ for every $N$, and the zero object has Tor amplitude in $[0,0]$. No constructibility or finiteness assumption on $A$ or $K$ is imposed.

proof.text: Apply the ringed-site results to $\mathcal C=Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $R=A_Y$, using a small site in the module-sheaf universe. For an arbitrary $N[0]$, choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to N[0]$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated], the functor $B\mapsto\operatorname{Tot}(B\otimes_R P)$ descends to $F_N:D(R)\to D(R)$, canonically identified with $K\mapsto K\otimes_A^L N$ of [def-weil-derived-tensor], and its integer-shift comparison gives $F_N(K[m])\cong F_N(K)[m]$. This is the first asserted isomorphism. It is natural in $K$ as a functor shift comparison. It is natural in $N$ as well: the fixed-tensor lemma states that transformations induced by chain maps between flat-term K-flat fixed arguments and by their localization commute with these comparisons; [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] identifies that localization with all of $D(R)$. Thus every derived morphism between the degree-zero coefficients, in particular every module-sheaf morphism $N\to N\prime$, satisfies the naturality square. The canonical identifications with derived tensor give independence of the chosen replacement. No boundedness or cohomological flatness has been assumed.

proof.text: Apply the cohomology functor $\mathcal H^i$ of [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] to the isomorphism in Step 1, then apply [lem-sp-derived-cohomology-shift] with the abelian category $\Mod(A_Y)$, $M=K\otimes_A^L N$, $k=m$, $a=i$, and $a\prime=i+m$. The required equation $k+a=a\prime$ holds by commutativity of integer addition. This gives $\mathcal H^i((K[m])\otimes_A^L N)\cong\mathcal H^{i+m}(K\otimes_A^L N)$. Naturality follows by composing the natural comparison in Step 1 with the cohomology-shift isomorphism, which is natural for all objects of the unbounded derived category.

proof.text:
Unfold Tor amplitude using [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. For each integer $i$, one has $i
otin[a-m,b-m]$ if and only if $i+m
otin[a,b]$. If $K$ has amplitude in $[a,b]$, the right-hand cohomology sheaf of Step 2 therefore vanishes for every $N$ and every $i
otin[a-m,b-m]$, proving the forward implication. Conversely, suppose $K[m]$ has amplitude in $[a-m,b-m]$. Given any $N$ and $j
otin[a,b]$, put $i=j-m$. Then $i
otin[a-m,b-m]$ and $i+m=j$, so Step 2 identifies $\mathcal H^j(K\otimes_A^L N)$ with zero. This is amplitude in $[a,b]$. Also $a-m\le b-m$ because $a\le b$. The argument covers every integer $m$, including negative $m$.

proof.text: Let $e:K\cong L$. For every $N$, use the functor $F_N$ of Step 1 supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated]. The maps $F_N(e)$ and $F_N(e^{-1})$ are inverse, because a functor preserves compositions and identities. Applying the cohomology functors of [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] gives isomorphisms $\mathcal H^i(K\otimes_A^L N)\cong\mathcal H^i(L\otimes_A^L N)$ for all $i$. An object is zero if and only if an isomorphic object is zero, by composing its universal maps with the isomorphism and inverse. Hence the vanishing tests in [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] are equivalent, with the same interval $[a,b]$ and all the same test sheaves $N$.

proof.text: For the resolution $P\to N[0]$ in Step 1, the fixed-tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated] computes $0\otimes_A^L N$ by $\operatorname{Tot}(0\otimes_R P)$. The formula of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] gives degree $r$ equal to $\bigoplus_{p+q=r}0\otimes_R P^q=0$: a bilinear map out of a zero factor is uniquely zero, so its tensor product is zero, and a coproduct of zero objects is zero. Its differentials are the unique maps between zero objects. Consequently this is the zero complex and represents the zero derived object. By the kernel/image formula in [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], all its cohomology sheaves vanish. In particular the tests outside $[0,0]$ in [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] vanish for every $N$, giving the last assertion.
